overview: A series of troughs and fronts keeps moving through the West. Snow and rain come in waves: Wednesday to Friday for the Sierra and Utah, Thursday to Saturday for the Rockies, and a weekend system for the Pacific Northwest.

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: A strong system brings heavy rain and mountain snow, with gusty south-southeast winds that favor the Sierra. Kirkwood leads with 69" total, its biggest day Thursday. Winter Storm Warning above 4000 feet runs from tonight until 4 AM Friday, with another from Tuesday. Forecasters expect a lighter weekend system before a more active pattern for Thanksgiving week.

regions.title: Eastern Sierra
regions.text: A winter storm brings heavy snow to the Sierra Wednesday through Friday, with strong, gusty winds. Mammoth has 50" total, with its biggest day Thursday. Snow levels drop Thursday, bringing snow to valley and foothill commutes in western Nevada. The NWS is calling for more, 62 to 86 inches over Wednesday through Sunday night. A Winter Storm Warning runs through Friday morning.

regions.title: Wasatch
regions.text: A longer storm arrives in pieces from Thursday through Saturday morning. Friday evening into Saturday, colder air should bring snow down to valley floors, with winds favoring the northern mountains. Snowbasin leads with 49" total, its biggest day Friday at 27". Freezing temperatures are likely in the Virgin River corridor near Zion Saturday and Sunday mornings.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: A cold front has moved east, and the Bighorns are getting the last of the snow today. A new trough arrives Thursday, bringing light snow to western Wyoming and Idaho. The main trough reaches Friday, with more widespread precipitation Friday night. Grand Targhee leads with 32" total, its biggest day Friday. Sun Valley sees Thursday's heaviest snow, with a possible winter weather advisory tonight.

regions.title: Southern Rockies
regions.text: A progressive trough brings snow to the Continental Divide, with a brief lull after that. Another system arrives Thursday night into Friday with light accumulations along the Divide. Saturday brings stronger wind and light rain or snow showers. Wolf Creek leads with 21" total, with its biggest day Monday. Cooler weather runs through the weekend, with another system possible Monday or Tuesday.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: Snow on the Divide tapers early Wednesday, with clearing skies and slick passes. A new storm brings snow to the mountains Thursday night through Saturday, with the best totals favoring the central Colorado mountains. Telluride leads with 12" total, with its biggest day Monday. Cold air keeps afternoon highs below normal, and desert valleys see their first freezing temperatures of the season.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: A low moving south brings mountain snow and lowland rain to Oregon today, with a breezy Blue Mountains. Dense fog is likely in the Columbia Basin into mid-morning. Mt. Bachelor leads with 10" total, with its biggest day Wednesday. Precipitation eases Thursday and Friday is mostly dry. The weekend brings another low, with snow levels near 2500 feet and likely snow on the passes.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
